newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. AFRICAN PARTIES TACKLE CONSTITUTIONAL DEADLOCK.
newsitem.headline: S. AFRICAN PARTIES TACKLE CONSTITUTIONAL DEADLOCK.

text.p: South African constitutional negotiators postponed public debate on Thursday for a renewed effort to break a deadlock over provincial police powers in a series of private meetings.

African National Congress (ANC) negotiator Pravin Gordhan told the all-party management committee of the Constitutional Assembly early on Thursday that talks had deadlocked around midnight on the management of municipal police forces.
The white-led National Party is demanding changes to the draft constitution adopted in May to increase provincial control over local police forces.

The ANC argues that this is not necessary to address the flaws identified by the Constitutional Court, which returned the draft constitution for more work on eight issues before it can be ratified and enacted.

Plans for two sub-committees to meet at 10 a.m. were shelved and Constitutional Development Minister Mohammed Valli Moosa told negotiators at the management committee meeting to go away and work on compromises before 2 p.m.

Moosa said it was important to stick to the timetable for adoption of the constitution on January 1, which would require committee-level accords on Thursday to prepare the way for ratification of an amended text on Friday next week.

Inkatha Freedom Party negotiators Walter Felgate and Peter Smith met ANC and NP delegates privately on Thursday for talks on a package of amendments to shift the focus of power from the central government towards the provinces.
Felgate told Reuters the ANC was receptive to Inkatha, but said it was too early to tell whether agreement was likely.
A senior Constitutional Assembly official told Reuters there was still little likelihood of concessions that would convince Inkatha to support the constitution.
He predicted that Inkatha, who returned to the talks on Tuesday after an 18-month boycott, would drop out before the end of next week.
